facts.name: Program and specializations
facts.detail: ECE department MSCompE page: specializations include VLSI systems, computer networks, embedded systems, machine learning, and scientific computing.
facts.quote: The areas of specialization include (but are not limited to) VLSI Systems, Computer Networks, Embedded Systems, Machine Learning and Scientific Computing.

facts.name: 30 units, Plan A or Plan B
facts.detail: Each student must complete 30 units under Plan A (thesis) or Plan B (project).
facts.quote: Each student must complete 30 units either by selecting Plan A (Thesis) or Plan B (Project).

facts.name: 600/700-level unit split
facts.detail: Eighteen of the 30 units should be 600- and 700-numbered courses; the remaining 12 may be 500-, 600-, or 700-level department courses.
facts.quote: Eighteen of the thirty units should be 600 and 700-numbered courses. The remaining twelve units can be from 500, 600 or 700-level courses offered by the department.

facts.name: Outside-department course limit
facts.detail: No more than two courses may be taken from other College of Engineering or College of Sciences departments, with prior Graduate Advisor approval.
facts.quote: No more than two courses can be taken from other departments in the College of Engineering or from the College of Sciences to satisfy these requirements, with the prior approval of the Graduate Advisor.

facts.name: Minimum 3.0 GPA to complete the degree
facts.detail: A minimum average GPA of 3.0 is required to complete the degree.
facts.quote: A minimum average GPA of 3.0 is required to successfully complete the degree.

facts.name: Plan A thesis units
facts.detail: Plan A: 21 units of coursework, 6 units of COMPE 797 Research, and 3 units of COMPE 799A Thesis.
facts.quote: Students opting for Plan A must complete 21 units of course work (7 courses), 6 units of COMPE 797 "Research" (typically as two 3-unit COMPE 797 “Research”, taken in two different semesters) and 3 units of COMPE 799A "Thesis" under supervision of a full-time ECE faculty.

facts.name: Plan B project units
facts.detail: Plan B: at least 18 units of depth-area courses and 3 units of COMPE 798 as the project.
facts.quote: Students opting for Plan B or the Project option are required to pick an area of specialization and complete a minimum of 18 units of “Depth Area Courses” and 3 units of COMPE 798 as the project.

facts.name: International in-person enrollment
facts.detail: International students needing an I-20 must enroll in at least 6 units of in-person instruction per semester and may not take more than 3 units fully online.
facts.quote: International Students requiring an I-20 immigration document from SDSU must be enrolled in a minimum of 6 units of in-person course instruction on campus, per semester. International students may not take more than 3 units of fully online course instruction, per semester.

facts.detail: Tentative spring list includes COMPE525 Cyber Physical Systems.

facts.name: Five 500-level courses allowed for MSCOMPE
facts.detail: Course-guidelines instructions: four 500-level courses are accepted for MSEE and five are allowed for MSCOMPE.
facts.quote: Four 500-level courses are accepted for the MSEE graduate program and five are allowed for the MSCOMPE program.

facts.name: Domestic classified admission
facts.detail: Department admission page (covers MSEE and MSCompE): domestic classified standing requires a bachelor's in Electrical or Computer Engineering from an ABET-accredited U.S. program and a 2.85 GPA in the last 60 semester (90 quarter) units of technical coursework.
facts.quote: Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Computer Engineering from an ABET accredited engineering program in the USA.

facts.name: Domestic technical GPA
facts.detail: Domestic classified standing also requires a minimum 2.85 GPA in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter units of technical coursework.
facts.quote: A minimum grade point average of 2.85 (based on 4.0 scale) in the last 60 semester (90 quarter) units of technical course work.

facts.name: International classified admission
facts.detail: International classified standing requires a bachelor's in Electrical, Electronics, Instrumentation, or Computer Engineering from a recognized program and an equivalent technical GPA of 3.0 or higher.
facts.quote: An equivalent grade point average of 3.0 (based on 4.0 scale) or higher in all technical course work.

facts.name: International English score
facts.detail: Program minimum TOEFL is 85 or IELTS 6.5, which the page says is higher than the university minimum.
facts.quote: A minimum TOEFL score of 85 or minimum IELTS score of 6.5. Please note that the minimum TOEFL score required by the program is higher than the minimum required score of the university.

facts.name: GRE not required (department admissions page)
facts.detail: Department admissions page: GRE scores are not required. The 2026–2027 catalog program page could not be fetched (AWS WAF), so a catalog GRE statement could not be compared.

facts.name: Statement of purpose not considered
facts.detail: The Electrical Engineering program statement on this shared MSEE & MSCompE admissions page says an SOP is not required and is not used in admission decisions.
facts.quote: The Electrical Engineering program does not require a Statement of Purpose (SOP) as it is not taken into consideration with making admission decisions. Please do not send an SOP.

facts.name: Unofficial transcripts and one letter of recommendation
facts.detail: Unofficial transcripts and one mandatory LOR are required for both MSEE and MSCompE applicants.
facts.quote: Unofficial transcripts and one mandatory LOR are required for both the MSEE and MSCompE degree applicants.

facts.name: Department page Fall 2026 application window
facts.detail: Department admissions page: the application window for Fall 2026 is October 1, 2025 to February 1, 2026. This disagrees in cycle/year with the university master's-degrees page for Fall 2027, quoted separately; both are reported, no winner is chosen.
facts.quote: The application window for Fall 2026 will be from October 1, 2025 to February 1, 2026.

facts.name: Department Cal State Apply date for that window
facts.detail: Department page: complete the university Cal State Apply application by February 1, 2026.
facts.quote: Complete the University Online Application via Cal State Apply – Must be completed by February 1, 2026.

facts.name: Department official documents date
facts.detail: Department page: official test scores and transcripts must be received by February 15, 2026.
facts.quote: Send official test scores and transcripts to Graduate Admissions – Must be received by February 15, 2026.

facts.name: Scholarship consideration date
facts.detail: Department page: applications received after January 15 will not be considered for resident tuition-waiver scholarships.
facts.quote: Applications received after JANUARY 15th will not be considered for scholarships.

facts.name: University page Fall 2027 Computer Engineering deadlines
facts.detail: University master's-degrees page, Computer Engineering, M.S. section: Fall 2027 Cal State Apply February 1, documents to Graduate Admissions February 15, program application February 15. This is a later cycle than the department page's Fall 2026 window; both are quoted.

facts.name: University Fall 2027 Cal State Apply date (CompE section)
facts.detail: In the Computer Engineering, M.S. section of the university page: Submit Cal State Apply Application: February 1 (under Fall 2027 Deadlines).
facts.quote: Submit Cal State Apply Application: February 1 Submit Documents to Graduate Admissions: February 15 Submit program application: February 15 Spring 2027 Deadlines Submit Cal State Apply Application: August 31

facts.name: University Spring 2027 Computer Engineering deadlines
facts.detail: University page CompE section lists Spring 2027 dates (Cal State Apply August 31; documents September 15; program application September 15). The department admissions page does not give these Spring 2027 dates.
facts.quote: Spring 2027 Deadlines Submit Cal State Apply Application: August 31 Submit Documents to Graduate Admissions : September 15 Submit program application: September 15 Contact Information Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
